blocks.text: A wireless access point provides Wi-Fi connectivity. It allows wireless devices to connect to a network (as shown in Figure 1.7). It extends wireless network coverage. Access points are used in large buildings and campuses. They improve signal strength and stability. Wireless access points support mobile connectivity.

blocks.alt: A wireless access point with an antenna sends Wi-Fi waves and signal beams to a mobile phone, a laptop and a desktop computer below it.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.7: Wireless Access Point (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.7).
